subject.title: [Bug]: exec tool silently corrupts 2>&1 / 2>/dev/null shell redirect arguments

question: Should maintainers queue a fix from the 2026.5.27 report alone, or first require a current-main repro that isolates the exact exec command mutation boundary?
rationale: The report is actionable, but current source and Codex dependency inspection show several paths preserving the command string, so choosing a fix layer without a fresh boundary risks patching the wrong subsystem.

options.title: Require current-main boundary proof
options.body: Keep the issue open and ask for or run a live current-main repro through the same user-facing exec path before dispatching a fix.

options.title: Queue exploratory repair anyway
options.body: Let a maintainer-owned investigation attempt a fix now, accepting that the first PR may mostly be diagnostic coverage rather than a direct repair.

options.title: Close as not reproduced
options.body: Close the issue because inspected source paths preserve the command string, but this would discard a plausible shipped regression without disproving it on the reported path.

recommendation.title: Require current-main boundary proof
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and ask for or run a live current-main repro through the same user-facing exec path before dispatching a fix.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history across exec naming, host execution, safe-bin trust, and redirect allowlist matching.
